review_notes: The principal question is whether joint national and city-office auditor industry expertise is associated with audit quality. Retain the authors’ primary fully controlled Model 3 for the paper’s three central outcome measures (absolute abnormal accruals, MEET, and going-concern opinion), for both specialist definitions. The abstract and Introduction identify all three outcomes as audit-quality tests; the authors call Model 3 the primary model of interest for Equation (4) and report it as Model 3 for Equations (5) and (6).

Excluded Equation (4) Models 1 and 2 because the paper identifies Model 3 as its primary test; excluded Table 6 income-increasing/income-decreasing abnormal-accrual decompositions because the paper explicitly labels these as robustness tests; excluded Fama–MacBeth, continuous-market-share interaction, size partitions, and other sensitivity analyses.

Equation (1) is retained as the sole supporting fitted construction because its coefficients generate expected total accruals used for DACC. Equation (2) applies those fitted coefficients algebraically and Equation (3) forms a difference; neither is an additional fitted regression.

Needs review remains for source-reported gaps: Equation (4) versus Table 3 give incompatible σ(CFO) windows; the paper does not specify the ΔREC scaling in Equation (2), Altman-score formula, or ROA operational formula; and the reported Rogers-style inference does not identify the correction or grouping dimension.
results_review_notes: Source-first verification confirms all 100 selected coefficient estimate and p-value pairs against the original tables. Table 5 uses source-labeled asymptotic t-statistics (Student-t reference; df not stated); Tables 7–8 use source-labeled Wald chi-square p-values (chi-square reference cannot be represented in the schema, so reference and df remain unknown). No coefficient SEs or individual test-statistic cells are reported. Table 5 Definition 1 and Table 7 footnote 29 coefficient comparisons are retained as auxiliary summaries of existing fits; missing numeric test fields and unclear scope remain explicit.
